h1: Steel Aircraft Hangars in Wyoming, Utah & Idaho
answer: Brooks Steel Buildings supplies custom pre-engineered steel aircraft hangars for private and corporate aircraft. Wide clear spans give you open floor for wings and tails, door openings are designed for your hangar door, and every building is engineered for your site’s snow and wind loads.
intro_p: A hangar starts with the aircraft: wingspan, tail height, and how you move it in and out. We design the clear span, eave height, and door opening around those dimensions, then engineer the building for your site. Explore dimensions, rooflines, colors, and openings in our 3D designer before you call. Planning a shop, warehouse, or other building at your airport? See our Industrial and Warehouse and Shops and Garages pages.

faq: What size hangar do I need?

Start with your aircraft’s wingspan, length, and tail height, then add room to move the aircraft in and out and to work around it. Tell us your aircraft and we will help you choose a width, depth, and eave height.
What types of hangar doors can the building be designed for?
We design the door opening for bi-fold, hydraulic, and sliding hangar doors. Tell us the door type and size you plan to use so the framing and clearances are designed correctly.
No. We design and frame the building for your hangar door, and the door is installed by others. Tell us the door type and opening size early so the design accounts for it.
Can you design a hangar with a wide clear span?

Yes. Clear-span steel buildings can be designed with wide, open floors and no interior columns. The practical size depends on your loads, site, and design. Tell us the size you need and we will plan the building around it.
Yes. We supply insulation. Tell us how you will use the hangar and we will include the right options in your quote.
Do I need airport or FAA approval for a hangar?

Requirements vary by airport and by county or city. Check with your airport authority and local building department before you order. Your building is engineered for local codes, with plans prepared for permitting.
Can I add on to the hangar later?
Yes. Steel buildings can often be designed so bays or lean-tos can be added later. Let us know your plans so the design allows for it.
How long does it take to get a hangar?
Our current turnaround is 8 to 10 weeks. Timelines can vary with project size, options, and demand.
